Chapter 12: The Ongoing Fight for Justice
Even though the legal system had delivered a verdict, the real fight for justice was still just beginning.
Chanel saw firsthand how the system let survivors down. She noticed how it seemed to protect the comfort of the accused, demanded impossible perfection from those who’d already been hurt, and left so many victims feeling completely betrayed and alone.
Instead of stepping back, she got involved—working with lawmakers, advocates, and other survivors to push for real change. She started speaking out about what really needs to happen: trauma-informed care, better training for judges and juries, and laws that actually put survivors’ needs at the center.
Most people don’t realize just how many barriers survivors run into. Things like endless paperwork, deeply personal and invasive questions, or facing disbelief and outright dismissal at every turn.
Chanel listened to story after story from people who’d been silenced—folks who felt like giving up, who’d been retraumatized by the very institutions meant to help them heal.
That’s when she realized something really important: justice isn’t just about punishment. It’s about healing. It’s about restoration. And it’s about building a world where survivors can actually thrive.
She became a passionate advocate for policies focused not just on fixing what’s broken, but on preventing harm in the first place, on education, and on real support for those who’ve been hurt.
The work was slow, and honestly, it was often frustrating. There were setbacks, disappointments, and moments when it felt like nothing would ever change.
But Chanel wouldn’t give up. She drew strength from the community—survivors and allies who stood with her—and from the knowledge that every single small victory made a difference.
